commit_reviews.summary: Session 5 adds rate limiting, history queries, and TTL cleanup that cleanly mirror the existing MessageStore/_get_redis/Response and background-task patterns already in the file.

compounding_issues: Single-file monolith persisted through all 5 sessions (app.py 600 lines, test_app.py 957 lines) — the greenfield choice to keep everything in one module was never split, constraining maintainability as features stacked.

Proliferation of module-level global singletons (_store_instance, _transport, _redis, registry, _server_id) — sessions 3-5 stacked new globals on session 1's global registry, forcing _reset_store/_set_redis/_reset_transport test fixtures to isolate state.
Silent 'except Exception: pass' fail-open pattern (Redis bridging, rate limiting, cleanup task) grew from session 3 through session 5, masking failures in production paths.
Session 3's _deliver_from_redis re-duplicated the broadcast send + dead-client unregister loop instead of reusing session 1/2 code; only session 4's transport extraction cleaned it up.
key_decisions: Session 1 full greenfield rewrite to an async WebSocket push architecture (websockets + asyncio) with a type-dispatched message handler, discarding the Flask seed rather than evolving it.
Session 2 adopted a channel pub/sub subscription model (subscribe/unsubscribe, channel-scoped broadcast, per-channel subscriber registry) as the core domain abstraction.
Session 3 added SQLite MessageStore persistence plus a Redis pub/sub bridge with _server_id echo-suppression for cross-server fan-out and message history.
Session 4 extracted a BaseTransport ABC (WebSocketTransport behind a TRANSPORT env switch) to decouple message delivery from websockets and centralize connection-error handling.
Session 5 introduced fail-open Redis-backed rate limiting, a TTL-based message retention cleanup task, and cursor-style history pagination with has_more.
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily across the arc. Session 1 established a clean, minimal, fully-tested core (8 tests); session 2 accreted channel features with tests scaling in lockstep (15); session 3 added persistence and distributed integration (24); session 4 was a disciplined behavior-preserving refactor that kept tests unchanged (24) while removing duplicated send/error logic; session 5 hardened the service operationally (32 tests). Every stage's suite passed (verified 8/8, 15/15, 24/24, 24/24, 32/32), indicating each session built on working state. The only flat spot was architectural: the file and global-state structure never evolved even as the code tripled in size.
story_review.summary: A highly coherent, well-tested five-session progression from a minimal WebSocket core to a production-hardened, Redis-integrated notification service, marred only by a persistent single-file/global-singleton structure.
